sentences.text: Annexure A5 order passed by the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Vadakara, refusing to discharge the accused Nos.1 to 3 in CC No.1369/2014 on the files of the said Court, is under challenge in this revision filed at the instance of accused Nos.2 and 3 in the said case.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Vadakara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The aforesaid case arose out of a private complaint filed by the 2nd respondent alleging the commission of offences under Sections 498A and 406 IPC.
The learned Magistrate took the complaint to files and issued summons to the accused.
The 1st accused is the husband of the 2nd respondent/complainant.
The 2nd and 3rd accused are her mother-in-law and brother-in-law respectively.
2. The allegation in the complaint is that the accused have been subjecting the complainant to cruelty by demanding more gold ornaments and money from her.
There are also allegations to the effect that the accused often resorted to innuendos and inflicted mental cruelty upon her.
3. In the course of procedure under Section 244 Cr.P.C, the learned Magistrate recorded the evidence of the complainant and her brother as PW1 and PW2 respectively.
While the case was posted for 2026:KER:19588 framing charges, the accused filed Annexure A4 discharge petition.
The dismissal of the above discharge petition, vide order dated 31.12.2016, is under challenge in this revision.
4. During the course of proceedings in this revision, the 1st revision petitioner was reported to be no more.

Since there was no representation from the part of the revision petitioners for several posting dates, Adv.Mr.Alex John Pulimood, was appointed as Amicus Curiae to represent the 2nd revision petitioner.
5. Heard the learned Amicus Curiae representing the 2nd revision petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.
Though notice was duly served to the 2nd respondent/complainant, she did not choose to appear or to advance any arguments.

2 6.

The learned Amicus Curiae pointed out that the Trial Court went wrong in declining to discharge the 2nd petitioner notwithstanding the fact that even the complaint did not contain specific allegations against him.

It is pointed out that apart from omnibus sweeping allegations, nothing has been stated in the complaint pointing to any specific overt act of the 2nd petitioner indulging in physical or mental cruelty upon the complainant.
Secondly, it is submitted that the complaint is hopelessly 2026:KER:19588 barred by limitation even as per the averments of the complainant in Annexure A1 complaint.

In support of the above arguments, the learned Amicus Curiae pointed out that, as per the averments in the complaint, the complainant had left her matrimonial residence on 30.01.2011, and thereafter she had no occasion to have any interaction with any of the accused.

The present complaint has been filed on 23.04.2013, which is after a period of 3 years and 3 months from the above date when the complainant had left the matrimonial residence and ceased to have contacts with the accused.
7. As already pointed out by the learned Amicus Curiae, the complaint does not contain any specific allegations of cruelty as against the 2nd petitioner.

Apart from the omnibus statement that all the accused resorted to mental cruelty upon her by innuendos and other oral statements, there is nothing pointing to any specific overt act as against the 2nd petitioner.

8. The decisions rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kahkashan Kausar and Ors v. State of Bihar and Ors [(2022) 6 SCC 599] and Rajesh Chaddha v. State of Uttar Pradesh [AIR 2025 SC 2836] are relied on by the learned Amicus Curiae in support of the 2026:KER:19588 argument that the Apex Court has strongly deprecated the practice of roping in the in-laws by raising frivolous and fictitious allegations of matrimonial cruelty against them.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar and Ors v. State of Bihar and Ors [(2022) 6 SCC 599]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Rajesh Chaddha v. State of Uttar Pradesh [AIR 2025 SC 2836]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regards the challenge regarding limitation, the learned Amicus Curiae has relied on the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sanapareddy Maheedhar and Ors v State of Andhra Pradesh and Ors.

entities.text: Sanapareddy Maheedhar and Ors v State of Andhra Pradesh and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: [(2007)13 SCC 165] in which it has been laid down that the question of limitation has to be looked into by the Trial Court and that the condonation of delay as envisaged under Section 473 Cr.P.C has to be resorted to only in such cases where the Trial Court is satisfied that the delay has been properly explained or it is necessary to do so in the interests of justice.
Adverting to the facts of this case, the learned Amicus Curiae pointed out that none of the above situations arise in the case on hand for condonation of delay.
9. On going through the case records, I am of the view that the arguments advanced by the learned Amicus Curiae are perfectly right.
It is also pertinent to note that even in the sworn testimony of PW1 and PW2, there are no specific allegations levelled against the 2nd petitioner herein.

Therefore,
the refusal of the court below to discharge the 2nd petitioner, is totally against the principles of law in this regard.
Needless to say, the 2026:KER:19588 prayer of discharge of the 2nd petitioner (3rd accused) from criminal prosecution against him for the offence under Section 498A IPC, deserves to be allowed.

In the result, the revision stands allowed in part as follows:
1) The proceedings against the 2nd petitioner (3rd accused) in CC No.1369/2014 on the files of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Vadakara, are hereby quashed.

As against the 1st petitioner/2nd accused, the Trial Court shall verify whether she is alive, and pass appropriate orders, if it is found that the 1st petitioner is no more.
3) It is made clear that there is absolutely no fetter for the Trial Court to proceed against the 1st accused in respect of the offence alleged in this case.
This Court places on record its appreciation for the valuable assistance rendered by the learned Amicus Curiae Adv.Mr.Alex John Pulimood in addressing the various legal aspects on this matter.
